# 📈 lunary **Open-source observability & prompt platform for LLMs** [website](https://lunary.ai) - [docs](https://lunary.ai/docs) - [self host](https://lunary.ai/docs/self-host) [![npm version](https://badge.fury.io/js/lunary.svg)](https://badge.fury.io/js/lunary) ![PyPI - Version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/llmonitor) ![GitHub last commit (by committer)](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/lunary-ai/lunary) ![GitHub commit activity (branch)](https://img.shields.io/github/commit-activity/w/lunary-ai/lunary)
## Features Lunary helps AI devs take their apps in production, with features such as: - 💵 Analytics (cost, token, latency, ..) - 🔍 Monitoring (logs, traces, user tracking, ..) - ⛩️ Prompt Templates (versioning, team collaboration, ..) - 🏷️ Creat fine-tuning datasets - 🖲️ Chat & feedback tracking - 🧪 Evaluations It also designed to be: - 🤖 Usable with any model, not just OpenAI - 📦 Easy to integrate (2 minutes) - 🧑‍💻 Simple to self-host ## Demo https://github.com/lunary-ai/lunary/assets/5092466/a2b4ba9b-4afb-46e3-9b6b-faf7ddb4a931 ## ⚙️ Integration Modules available for: - [JavaScript](https://github.com/lunary-ai/lunary-js) - [Python](https://github.com/lunary-ai/lunary-py) Lunary natively supports: - [LangChain](https://lunary.ai/docs/langchain) (JS & Python) - [OpenAI module](https://lunary.ai/docs/js/openai) - [LiteLLM](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/observability/lunary_integration) Additionally you can use it with any framework by wrapping the relevant methods. ## 📚 Documentation Full documentation is available [on the website](https://lunary.ai/docs/intro). ## ☁️ Hosted version We offer [a hosted version](https://lunary.ai) with a free plan of up to 1k requests / days. With the hosted version: - 👷 don't worry about devops or managing updates - 🙋 get priority 1:1 support with our team --- counts --- 80 tsx 80 ts 13 json 5 md 4 woff2 4 gitignore 3 js 3 css 1 zshrc 1 zprofile 1 vscode 1 sql 1 ripgreprc 1 profile 1 prettierrc 1 idea 1 gitmodules 1 gitconfig 1 example 1 dockerignore 1 bashrc 1 bash_profile

     1	import type { FilterLogic, FilterParam } from "."
     2	import { FILTERS } from "."
     3	
     4	// because dots are used to separate filter parameters, we need to encode them
     5	const encode = (str: string) => encodeURIComponent(str).replace(/\./g, "%2E")
     6	
     7	const paramSerializer = (param: FilterParam, value: any) => {
     8	  if (value == undefined) {
     9	    return undefined
    10	  }
    11	  switch (param.type) {
    12	    case "select":
    13	      if (param.multiple) {
    14	        if (!value.length) return undefined
    15	        return value.map(encode).join(",")
    16	      } else {
    17	        return encode(value)
    18	      }
    19	    case "text":
    20	    case "number":
    21	      return encode(value)
    22	    case "date":
    23	      // get timestamp
    24	      return encode(value.getTime())
    25	    default:
    26	      return undefined
    27	  }
    28	}
    29	
    30	function deserializeParamValue(
    31	  filterParam: FilterParam,
    32	  v: string,
    33	): any | undefined {
    34	  switch (filterParam.type) {
    35	    case "select":
    36	      if (filterParam.multiple) {
    37	        return v.split(",").map(decodeURIComponent)
    38	      } else {
    39	        return decodeURIComponent(v)
    40	      }
    41	    case "text":
    42	      return decodeURIComponent(v)
    43	    case "number":
    44	      return Number(v)
    45	    case "date":
    46	      return new Date(Number(v))
    47	    default:
    48	      return undefined
    49	  }
    50	}
    51	
    52	// This function serializes the filter parameters for storage or transmission
    53	// Example:
    54	// ['AND', {id: 'type', params: {type: 'llm'}}, {id: 'tags', params: {tags: ['some', 'tags']}}]
    55	// Will be serialized to:
    56	// type=llm&tags=some.tags
    57	
    58	export function serializeLogic(logic: FilterLogic): string {
    59	  const serializeParamValue = (param: any): string => {
    60	    if (Array.isArray(param)) {
    61	      const all = param.map(serializeParamValue)
    62	
    63	      if (all.some((f) => typeof f !== "undefined")) return ""
    64	      return all.join(".")
    65	    } else if (
    66	      param &&
    67	      typeof param === "object" &&
    68	      param.params &&
    69	      !Object.values(param.params).some((f) => typeof f === "undefined")
    70	    ) {
    71	      const data = Object.entries(param.params)
    72	        .map(([key, value]) => {
    73	          const filterParam = FILTERS.find(
    74	            (filter) => filter.id === param.id,
    75	          )?.params.find((param) => (param as FilterParam).id === key)
    76	
    77	          if (!filterParam || filterParam.type === "label") {
    78	            return ""
    79	          }
    80	
    81	          return paramSerializer(filterParam, value)
    82	        })
    83	        .filter((serializedValue) => serializedValue !== "")
    84	        .join(".")
    85	
    86	      if (!data) return ""
    87	
    88	      return param.id + "=" + data
    89	    }
    90	    return ""
    91	  }
    92	
    93	  return logic
    94	    .map(serializeParamValue)
    95	    .filter((f) => f)
    96	    .join("&")
    97	}

    99	export function deserializeLogic(logicString: string): FilterLogic | undefined {
   100	  const deserializeParam = (param: string): any => {
   101	    const [id, params] = param.split("=")
   102	    const filter = FILTERS.find((filter) => filter.id === id)
   103	
   104	    if (!filter) {
   105	      return undefined
   106	    }
   107	
   108	    const filterParams = filter.params.filter(

   187	type ChunkResult = {
   188	  choices: { message: any }[]
   189	  tokens: number
   190	}
   191	
   192	async function handleStream(
   193	  stream: ReadableStream,
   194	  onNewToken: (data: ChunkResult) => void,
   195	  onComplete: () => void,
   196	  onError: (e: Error) => void,
   197	) {
   198	  try {
   199	    let tokens = 0
   200	    let choices: any[] = []
   201	    let res: ChunkResult
   202	    for await (const part of stream) {
   203	      // 1 chunk = 1 token
   204	      tokens += 1
   205	
   206	      const chunk = part.choices[0]
   207	
   208	      const { index, delta } = chunk
   209	
   210	      const { content, function_call, role, tool_calls } = delta
   211	
   212	      if (!choices[index]) {
   213	        choices.splice(index, 0, {
   214	          message: { role, content, function_call, tool_calls: [] },
   215	        })
   216	      }
   217	
   218	      if (content) choices[index].message.content += content || ""
   219	
   220	      if (role) choices[index].message.role = role
   221	
   222	      if (function_call?.name)
   223	        choices[index].message.function_call.name = function_call.name
   224	
   225	      if (function_call?.arguments)
   226	        choices[index].message.function_call.arguments +=
   227	          function_call.arguments
   228	
   229	      if (tool_calls) {
   230	        for (const tool_call of tool_calls) {
   231	          const existingCallIndex = choices[index].message.tool_calls.findIndex(
   232	            (tc) => tc.index === tool_call.index,
   233	          )
   234	
   235	          if (existingCallIndex === -1) {
   236	            choices[index].message.tool_calls.push(tool_call)
   237	          } else {
   238	            const existingCall =
   239	              choices[index].message.tool_calls[existingCallIndex]
   240	
   241	            if (tool_call.function?.arguments) {
   242	              existingCall.function.arguments += tool_call.function.arguments
   243	            }
   244	          }
   245	        }
   246	      }
   247	
   248	      res = {
   249	        choices,
   250	        tokens,
   251	      }
   252	
   253	      onNewToken(res)
   254	    }
   255	
   256	    // remove the `index` property from the tool_calls if any
   257	    // as it's only used to help us merge the tool_calls
   258	    choices = choices.map((c) => {
   259	      if (c.message.tool_calls) {
   260	        c.message.tool_calls = c.message.tool_calls.map((tc) => {
   261	          const { index, ...rest } = tc
   262	          return rest
   263	        })
   264	      }
   265	      return c
   266	    })
   267	
   268	    res = {
   269	      choices,
   270	      tokens,
   271	    }
   272	
   273	    onNewToken(res)
   274	
   275	    onComplete()
   276	  } catch (error) {
   277	    console.error(error)
   278	    onError(error)
   279	  }

   187	type ChunkResult = {
   188	  choices: { message: any }[]
   189	  tokens: number
   190	}
   191	
   192	async function handleStream(
   193	  stream: ReadableStream,
   194	  onNewToken: (data: ChunkResult) => void,
   195	  onComplete: () => void,
   196	  onError: (e: Error) => void,
   197	) {
   198	  try {
   199	    let tokens = 0
   200	    let choices: any[] = []
   201	    let res: ChunkResult
   202	    for await (const part of stream) {
   203	      // 1 chunk = 1 token
   204	      tokens += 1
   205	
   206	      const chunk = part.choices[0]
   207	
   208	      const { index, delta } = chunk
   209	
   210	      const { content, function_call, role, tool_calls } = delta
   211	
   212	      if (!choices[index]) {
   213	        choices.splice(index, 0, {
   214	          message: { role, content, function_call, tool_calls: [] },
   215	        })
   216	      }
   217	
   218	      if (content) choices[index].message.content += content || ""
   219	
   220	      if (role) choices[index].message.role = role
   221	
   222	      if (function_call?.name)
   223	        choices[index].message.function_call.name = function_call.name
   224	
   225	      if (function_call?.arguments)
   226	        choices[index].message.function_call.arguments +=
   227	          function_call.arguments
   228	
   229	      if (tool_calls) {
   230	        for (const tool_call of tool_calls) {
   231	          const existingCallIndex = choices[index].message.tool_calls.findIndex(
   232	            (tc) => tc.index === tool_call.index,
   233	          )
   234	
   235	          if (existingCallIndex === -1) {
   236	            choices[index].message.tool_calls.push(tool_call)
   237	          } else {
   238	            const existingCall =
   239	              choices[index].message.tool_calls[existingCallIndex]
   240	
   241	            if (tool_call.function?.arguments) {
   242	              existingCall.function.arguments += tool_call.function.arguments
   243	            }
   244	          }
   245	        }
   246	      }
   247	
   248	      res = {
   249	        choices,
   250	        tokens,
   251	      }
   252	
   253	      onNewToken(res)
   254	    }

   258	    choices = choices.map((c) => {

   271	    }

   274

     4	export async function getDatasetById(datasetId: string, projectId: string) {
     5	  const [dataset] =
     6	    await sql`select * from dataset where  id = ${datasetId} and project_id = ${projectId}`
     7	
     8	  if (!dataset) {
     9	    throw new Error("Dataset not found")
    10	  }
    11	
    12	  dataset.prompts =
    13	    await sql`select * from dataset_prompt where dataset_id = ${datasetId} order by created_at asc`
    14	
    15	  for (const prompt of dataset.prompts) {
    16	    prompt.variations =
    17	      await sql`select * from dataset_prompt_variation where prompt_id = ${prompt.id} order by created_at asc`
    18	  }
    19	
    20	  return dataset
    21	}

    24	export async function getDatasetBySlug(slug: string, projectId: string) {
    25	  const rows = await sql`
    26	    select
    27	      d.id as id,
    28	      d.project_id as project_id,
    29	      d.slug as slug,
    30	      p.id as prompt_id,
    31	      d.owner_id as owner_id,
    32	      p.messages as prompt_messages,
    33	      pv.id as variation_id,
    34	      pv.variables,
    35	      pv.context,
    36	      pv.ideal_output,
    37	      pv.context
    38	    from
    39	      dataset d 
    40	      left join dataset_prompt p on d.id = p.dataset_id
    41	      left join dataset_prompt_variation pv on pv.prompt_id = p.id
    42	    where 
    43	      d.slug = ${slug}
    44	      and d.project_id = ${projectId}
    45	    `
    46	
    47	  const { id, ownerId } = rows[0]
    48	  const dataset = {
    49	    id,
    50	    slug,
    51	    ownerId,
    52	    projectId,
    53	    items: [],
    54	  }
    55	
    56	  for (const { promptMessages, variables, idealOutput, context } of rows) {
    57	    const item = {
    58	      input: compileChatMessages(promptMessages, variables),
    59	      idealOutput,
    60	      context,
    61	    }
    62	    dataset.items.push(item)
    63	  }
    64	
    65	  return dataset
    66	}

    27	      d.id as id,

    33	      pv.id as variation_id,
    34	      pv.variables,
    35	      pv.context,
    36	      pv.ideal_output,
    37	      pv.context
    38	    from
    39	      dataset d 
    40	      left join dataset_prompt p on d.id = p.dataset_id
    41	      left join dataset_prompt_variation pv on pv.prompt_id = p.id
    42	    where 
    43	      d.slug = ${slug}
    44	      and d.project_id = ${projectId}
    45	    `
    46	
    47	  const { id, ownerId } = rows[0]
    48	  const dataset = {

    52	    projectId,
    53	    items: [],

    55	
    56	  for (const { promptMessages, variables, idealOutput, context } of rows) {

    64

    50	export const uuidFromSeed = async (seed: string): Promise<string> => {
    51	  const encoder = new TextEncoder()
    52	  const data = encoder.encode(seed)
    53	  const hash = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", data)
    54	  const hashArray = Array.from(new Uint8Array(hash))
    55	  const hashHex = hashArray.map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("")
    56	  return (
    57	    hashHex.substring(0, 8) +
    58	    "-" +
    59	    hashHex.substring(8, 12) +
    60	    "-" +
    61	    "4" +
    62	    hashHex.substring(13, 16) +
    63	    "-a" +
    64	    hashHex.substring(17, 20) +
    65	    "-" +
    66	    hashHex.substring(20, 32)
    67	  )
    68	}

    86	  } else if (typeof item === "function" || item !== Object(item)) {
    87	    return item
    88	  }
    89	  return Object.fromEntries(
    90	    Object.entries(item as Record<string, unknown>).map(
    91	      ([key, value]: [string, unknown]) => [
    92	        key.replace(/([-_][a-z])/gi, (c) =>
    93	          c.toUpperCase().replace(/[-_]/g, ""),

   122	): Promise<void> => {
   123	  // create parent thread run if it doesn't exist
   124	
   125	  const {

   128	    parentRunId,
   129	    feedback,

   131	    timestamp,
   132	  } = run

   135	
   136	  const coreMessage = clearUndefined({
   137	    role,
   138	    content,
   139	    extra,
   140	  })
   141	
   142	  if (typeof parentRunId === "undefined") {
   143	    throw new Error("parentRunId is undefined")
   144	  }
   145	
   146	  // Now you can safely use parentRunId in your
   147	
   148	  const [result] = await sql`
   149	    INSERT INTO run ${sql(
   150	      clearUndefined({
   151	        id: parentRunId,
   152	        type: "thread",
   153	        projectId,
   154	        externalUserId,
   155	        tags: threadTags,
   156	        input: coreMessage,
   157	      }),
   158	    )}
   159	    ON CONFLICT (id)
   160	    DO UPDATE SET
   161	      project_id = EXCLUDED.project_id,
   162	      external_user_id = EXCLUDED.external_user_id,
   163	      tags = EXCLUDED.tags,
   164	      input = EXCLUDED.input
   165	    RETURNING *
   166	  `
   167	
   168	  if (!result) {
   169	    throw new Error("Error upserting run")
   170	  }
   171	
   172	  // Reconciliate messages with runs
   173	  //
   174	  // 1 run can store 1 exchange ([system, user] -> [bot, tool])
   175	  //
   176	  // if previousRun and not retry_of
   177	  //     if this is bot message, then append to previous output's array
   178	  //     if this is user message:
   179	  //         if previous run output has bot then create new run and add to input array
   180	  //         if previous run is user, then append to previous input array
   181	  // else if retry_of
   182	  //     copy previousRun data into new run with new id, set `sibling_of` to previousRun, clear output, then:
   183	  //        if bot message: set output with [message]
   184	  //        if user message: also replace input with [message]
   185	  // else
   186	  //     create new run with either input or output depending on role
   187	  // note; in any case, update the ID to the latest received
   188	
   189	  // check if previous run exists. for that, look at the last run of the thread
   190	
   191	  const [previousRun] = await sql`
   192	    SELECT * FROM run
   193	    WHERE parent_run_id = ${parentRunId!}
   194	    ORDER BY created_at DESC
   195	    LIMIT 1`
   196	
   197	  const OUTPUT_TYPES = ["assistant", "tool", "bot"]
   198	  const INPUT_TYPES = ["user", "system"] // system is mostly used for giving context about the user
   199	
   200	  const shared = clearUndefined({
   201	    id,
   202	    projectId,
   203	    tags,
   204	    extra,
   205	    externalUserId,
   206	    feedback,
   207	  })
   208	
   209	  let update: any = {} // todo: type
   210	  let operation = "insert"
   211	
   212	  if (previousRun) {
   213	    // Those are computed columns, so we need to remove them
   214	    delete previousRun.inputText
   215	    delete previousRun.outputText
   216	    delete previousRun.errorText
   217	    delete previousRun.duration
   218	
   219	    if (isRetry) {
   220	      // copy previousRun data into new run with new id, set `sibling_of` to previousRun, clear output, then:
   221	      // if bot message: set output with [message]
   222	      // if user message: also replace input with [message]
   223	      update = {

   227	        output: OUTPUT_TYPES.includes(role) ? [coreMessage] : null,
   228	        input: INPUT_TYPES.includes(role) ? [coreMessage] : previousRun.input,
   229	      }
   230	
   231	      delete update.id // remove id to force using new one
   232	
   233	      operation = "insert"
   234	    } else if (OUTPUT_TYPES.includes(role)) {
   235	      // append coreMessage to output (if if was an array, otherwise create an array)
   236	
   237	      update.output = [...(previousRun.output || []), coreMessage]
   238	
   239	      operation = "update"
   240	    } else if (INPUT_TYPES.includes(role)) {
   241	      if (previousRun.output) {
   242	        // if last is bot message, create new run with input array
   243	
   244	        update.input = [coreMessage]
   245	        operation = "insert"
   246	      } else {
   247	        // append coreMessage to input (if if was an array, otherwise create an array)
   248	
   249	        update.input = [...(previousRun.input || []), coreMessage]
   250	
   251	        operation = "update"
   252	      }
   253	    }
   254	  } else {
   255	    // create new run with either input or output depending on role
   256	    if (OUTPUT_TYPES.includes(role)) {
   257	      update.output = [coreMessage]
   258	    } else if (INPUT_TYPES.includes(role)) {
   259	      update.input = [coreMessage]
   260	    }
   261	    operation = "insert"
   262	  }

   266	    update.createdAt = timestamp
   267	    update.endedAt = timestamp
   268	    update.parentRunId = run.parentRunId
   269	
   270	    await sql`
   271	      INSERT INTO run ${sql({ ...shared, ...update })}
   272	    `
   273	  } else if (operation === "update") {
   274	    update.endedAt = timestamp
   275	
   276	    await sql`
   277	      UPDATE run SET ${sql({ ...shared, ...update })} WHERE id = ${

   279	      }
   280	    `
   281	  }

    50	export const uuidFromSeed = async (seed: string): Promise<string> => {
    51	  const encoder = new TextEncoder()
    52	  const data = encoder.encode(seed)
    53	  const hash = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", data)
    54	  const hashArray = Array.from(new Uint8Array(hash))
    55	  const hashHex = hashArray.map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("")
    56	  return (
    57	    hashHex.substring(0, 8) +
    58	    "-" +
    59	    hashHex.substring(8, 12) +
    60	    "-" +
    61	    "4" +
    62	    hashHex.substring(13, 16) +
    63	    "-a" +
    64	    hashHex.substring(17, 20) +
    65	    "-" +
    66	    hashHex.substring(20, 32)
    67	  )
    68	}

   163	      tags = EXCLUDED.tags,

   174	  // 1 run can store 1 exchange ([system, user] -> [bot, tool])

   178	  //     if this is user message:

   180	  //         if previous run is user, then append to previous input array
   181	  // else if retry_of

   184	  //        if user message: also replace input with [message]

    22	function jaccardIndexSimilarity(str1: string, str2: string) {
    23	  // Tokenize the strings into sets of words
    24	  const set1 = new Set(str1.split(/\s+/))
    25	  const set2 = new Set(str2.split(/\s+/))
    26	
    27	  // Find the intersection of two sets
    28	  const intersection = new Set([...set1].filter((x) => set2.has(x)))
    29	
    30	  // Find the union of two sets
    31	  const union = new Set([...set1, ...set2])
    32	
    33	  // Calculate Jaccard Index
    34	  const jaccardIndex = intersection.size / union.size
    35	
    36	  // Scale to 1-100
    37	  const scaledJaccardIndex = 1 + jaccardIndex * (100 - 1)
    38	
    39	  return scaledJaccardIndex
    40	}

Audit complete. `findings.json` is written at the repo root (the only file I created; no source files touched). 21 findings across the Lunary backend and frontend.

## What dominates this codebase: broken multi-tenancy

**The root cause (CWE-306)** — `packages/backend/src/api/v1/auth/utils.ts:76`: `publicRoutes` contains the unanchored regex `/v1/datasets/.+`, and the middleware tests it against `ctx.path` with no regard for HTTP method. That makes *every* dataset endpoint — including all the DELETE and PATCH handlers — reachable with no JWT at all. The same middleware also assigns `ctx.state.projectId` straight from the bearer token without ever checking it against the `api_key` table, so a project's "public" key (which is literally the project UUID, embedded in browser SDK code) unlocks private dataset reads.

**Amplified by 9 dataset handlers** that never filter on `project_id` (`datasets/index.ts`) — unauthenticated read, overwrite, insert and delete of any tenant's prompts, variations and ideal outputs.

**Prompt-template takeover** — `templateVersions.ts:57` lets any logged-in user `PATCH /v1/template_versions/<n>` on another org's template, and the IDs are sequential `serial` integers (`init.sql:163`). Because SDKs pull the latest non-draft version, the attacker's text becomes the victim's production prompt. `templates.ts:113` gives the same result by appending a new version.

**Other unscoped ID lookups** — recursive run trees (`runs/index.ts:239`, deliberately scoped on the sibling route but not here), end-user PII over sequential IDs (`external-users.ts:70`), evaluation results, and project delete/rename across orgs.

## Two auth findings worth separate attention

- `auth/index.ts:117` — `signupMethod: "join"` takes `orgId` from the body and creates a `verified: true` member. No invitation record, no expiry, no revocation; the "invite" is a permanent org UUID link (`team.tsx:53`), and the seat check is client-side only.
- `auth/index.ts:194` — password reset validates only the JWT signature. It never compares against the `recovery_token` it stored for that purpose, so links are replayable; and since `signJwt` emits no purpose claim, a 30-day *session* token is accepted as a reset token, escalating a leaked session into account takeover.

## SSRF
`next.config.js:16` allows `hostname: "**"`, and attacker-controlled `image_url` values arrive via the unauthenticated ingest endpoint and flow into `next/image` (`Message.tsx:139`) — so viewing a logged run makes the Next.js server fetch an arbitrary host and relay the response.

Two notes on what I did **not** find, since they were in scope: no SQL injection is reachable — the `postgres.js` tagged templates parameterise all check-runner values, and the `sql(field + "_text")` calls go through identifier escaping (`checks/index.ts:193-253` is malformed and error-prone, e.g. `'${date}'` renders a literal `$1`, but not injectable). No XSS either: React escapes all run content, and the single `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (`Layout/Analytics.tsx:52`) is fed a build-time env var. There is no XML parsing, deserialization, or filesystem/shell access anywhere in first-party code.

- `auth/index.ts:117` — `signupMethod: "join"` takes `orgId` from the body and creates a `verified: true` member. No invitation record, no expiry, no revocation; the "invite" is a permanent org UUID link (`team.tsx:53`), and the seat check is client-side only.
- `auth/index.ts:194` — password reset validates only the JWT signature. It never compares against the `recovery_token` it stored for that purpose, so links are replayable; and since `signJwt` emits no purpose claim, a 30-day *session* token is accepted as a reset token, escalating a leaked session into account takeover.

## SSRF
`next.config.js:16` allows `hostname: "**"`, and attacker-controlled `image_url` values arrive via the unauthenticated ingest endpoint and flow into `next/image` (`Message.tsx:139`) — so viewing a logged run makes the Next.js server fetch an arbitrary host and relay the response.

Two notes on what I did **not** find, since they were in scope: no SQL injection is reachable — the `postgres.js` tagged templates parameterise all check-runner values, and the `sql(field + "_text")` calls go through identifier escaping (`checks/index.ts:193-253` is malformed and error-prone, e.g. `'${date}'` renders a literal `$1`, but not injectable). No XSS either: React escapes all run content, and the single `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (`Layout/Analytics.tsx:52`) is fed a build-time env var. There is no XML parsing, deserialization, or filesystem/shell access anywhere in first-party code.
